Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

development noun

growth, progress

also child development, progress made

classical

Cic. Tusc. 4.44: in suīs studiīs tantōs prōgressūs … facere
Cic. N. D. 1.15 (Lewis & Short)

prōgressus, prōgressūs m.

noun, fourth declension

progress, development

Progress made in learning or a skill: prōgressūs facere. Latin often says it with a verb: quantum prōfēcerit, how far he has come on; crēscit, he is growing (see develop).

Examples

  • in quō quantum esset animī, quantum ingeniī, quantum jam etiam prōfectūs, sermō prīmus ostendit

    our first conversation showed how much spirit and talent he had, and how far he had already come onSen. Ep. 11.1

  • jam tibi discipulus crēscit cicarō meus. jam quattuor partīs dīcit

    my little lad is growing into a pupil: he can already divide by fourPetr. 46.1

  • Quid ego vītium ortūs, satūs, incrēmenta commemorem?

    Why should I tell of the vines’ sprouting, planting and growth?Cic. Sen. 52

Other words

  • prōfectus, prōfectūs m. — progress, improvement

    noun, fourth declension · also used · classical · Sen. Ep. 11.1: quantum jam etiam prōfectūs; Sen. Ep. 20.1: experīmentum prōfectūs tuī

    From prōficiō; in Ovid and post-Augustan prose (Lewis & Short).

  • incrēmentum, incrēmentī n. — growth, increase

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Cic. Sen. 52: vītium ortūs, satūs, incrēmenta

    Of plants and animals growing, and of anything that increases.

See also develop, develop, grow, increase.
